source_documents.title: New Insights into Intersystem Crossing in Substituted Aromatics: Singlet–Triplet Conversion in Carbonyl-Substituted Anthracenes

reference_evidence_units.quote: 9AA is a minimally fluorescent compound at room temperature (for example, Φf = 2 × 10−4 in cyclohexane, see Table 1) which is typical for molecules with a fast S1 depopulation channel.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 9AA vs 2AA
reference_evidence_units.statement: 9AA is nearly dark while 2AA fluoresces strongly (0.04-0.8).

reference_evidence_units.quote: The time-resolved signals from 9AA show that ISC takes place after spectral shifts that reflect the evolution of the carbonyl group to a slanted geometry as it adjusts to a dihedral angle of around 40° with respect to the aromatic plane. Depending on the solvent, in 9AA manifold crossing takes place on the 3 to 25 ps time-scale.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 9AA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: femtosecond fluorescence upconversion and TA, several solvents
reference_evidence_units.statement: ISC in 3-25 ps follows a sub-ps carbonyl reorientation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In summary, for 9acetylanthracene (9AA) the S1(1La) state undergoes at least partial structural relaxation without crossings with other singlets, and remains of emissive ππ* character (1La) throughout this path.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 9AA
reference_evidence_units.statement: S1 stays pi-pi* (no singlet n-pi* crossing).

reference_evidence_units.quote: uch effect is related to the energy-coincidence of the singlet−triplet pair and to the switch-on of spin−orbit couplings related the nonparallel orientation of bonds localized in the aromatic plane and those associated with the tilted substituent double bonds.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 9AA
reference_evidence_units.statement: Near-degenerate S1/T(n-pi*-mixed) pair and SOC switched on by the tilted carbonyl.

reference_evidence_units.quote: When the acetyl group corresponds to anthracene position 2 as in the case of 2-acetylanthracene (2AA), the near planarity of the substituent effectively corresponds with reduced couplings with the triplet manifold and much longer fluorescent state lifetime of up to 15 ns.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2AA (comparison)
reference_evidence_units.statement: The coplanar 2-isomer has weak triplet coupling and a long-lived fluorescent S1.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
reference_mechanisms.rationale: S1 decays by intersystem crossing in 3-25 ps (solvent dependent) after the acetyl group tilts to about 40 degrees; SOC switched on by the tilted carbonyl and a near-degenerate triplet; the coplanar 2-isomer, with weak triplet coupling, fluoresces for up to 15 ns.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The acetyl torsion (sub-ps) precedes ISC, but the paper attributes the dark S1 to orientation-dependent spin-orbit coupling, not to free or restricted motion.
